title: Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read GEO metadata for all five series. GSE279411 (bulk RNA-seq) has 12 samples; GSE319937 (bulk RNA-seq) has 18. Opened GSE319937_TPM_values.csv.gz: 57,500 genes x 18 samples (6 conditions x 3 replicates), with Ensembl IDs and gene names. GSE279410 (ChIP-seq, chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing) lists 27+ samples; GSE326624 lists 6 samples plus 2 averaged bigWig signal tracks. GSE324238 (single-nucleus multiome) is 2 mice: Vehicle and CTPI2 (an inhibitor of the citrate carrier SLC25A1) .h5 matrices, 62.5 MB each, a 1.52 GB Seurat object and a 5.1 GB RAW tar, all checked by HEAD only.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Experimental design (irradiation-induced senescence in IMR90 fibroblasts, CCCP mitochondrial clearance, acetate/mtDNA rescue, aged-mouse CTPI2 treatment) and the source-data tables, which are figure-level summaries and were not retrieved. The supplement listing timed out.

a1_downloadable.note: All GEO series are public and the processed TPM/count files download (verified for GSE319937).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only labels are experimental condition names in sample headers (e.g. Prol, IR, IR.CCCP). No measured per-item outcome column exists for a prediction task; any gene-level label (for example 'is a SASP gene') would have to be built from curated lists.

a3_inputs_present.note: Expression matrices with Ensembl gene IDs are present in the files.

a4_units_stated.note: Files are named TPM (transcripts per million) and raw counts.

a5_enough_rows.note: The bulk RNA-seq sets have 12 + 18 = 30 samples (verified), and the multiome set has 2 animals. That is far below 400 labelled units; the many cells in the multiome all come from one vehicle and one treated mouse.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~130 MB for bulk TPM plus the two .h5 matrices
a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed matrices fit; the 5.1 GB raw tar is unnecessary.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 18 GSE319937 columns match its stated design of 6 conditions x 3 replicates.

a8_label_provenance.note: Conditions are experimental interventions, not model outputs.

existing_models.name: SenCID (senescence identification from transcriptomes; trained on 52 datasets, 602 samples, 30 cell types)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond the search snippet.

existing_models.name: DeepScence (deep neural network for senescent cells in single-cell and spatial data, Cell Genomics)
SenCat logistic-regression senescence scores (14 primary cell types, 30+ senescence paradigms, Molecular Cell 2026)

backbone.name: Geneformer or scGPT (single-cell foundation models) could embed the multiome cells
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible for ~tens of thousands of cells
backbone.licence: Apache-2.0 (Geneformer); not checked for this use

integration.partner_dataset: GTEx (tissue gene expression), joinable on Ensembl gene ID
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None strong: 30 bulk samples cannot support a learned model, and the join would only annotate genes.

controls.positive_control: SASP genes such as IL6 and CXCL8 rising from Prol to IR samples
controls.external_validation: SenCat or the SenCID compendium of senescence transcriptomes

honest_claim_h3: With 30 bulk samples from one fibroblast line and two mice, a model could only separate the authors' own treatment conditions, which differential expression already does.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene expression of senescent cells to predict whether mitochondrial metabolism is intact or blocked.
plain_idea.train_on: Bulk RNA-seq profiles of IMR90 fibroblasts under 6 conditions in triplicate (18 samples, verified), plus 12 more from a second set.
plain_idea.predict: The experimental condition (proliferating, senescent, mitochondria-depleted, rescued), which is known from the lab design.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: the condition is known by design and 30 samples are too few to learn a general rule; existing senescence classifiers already cover this.

more_or_better_data.why: We have 30 bulk samples; SenCID was trained on 602 samples from 52 datasets.

confidence_score.why: Triplicates give per-condition noise, but too few conditions to calibrate a predictor.

models_beatable.why: Recent (2024-2026) senescence classifiers exist and reportedly reach very high accuracy on bulk data; there is nothing to beat with 30 samples.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Adding 30 samples measured in one cell line would not make better predictions near-certain.

ml_idea: Classify mitochondrial or acetyl-CoA perturbation states from senescent-cell transcriptomes. Not viable at n = 30.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from verified file sizes; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count GEO samples: 12 + 18 bulk RNA-seq and 2 multiome mice, done, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic paper with 30 bulk RNA-seq samples (verified) and 2 multiome mice; the only labels are treatment conditions (fails A2/A5), and senescence classifiers like SenCID already exist.
